text: Everpeak Software has 40,000 paying accounts on annual contracts, and right now, Customer Success only learns an account is leaving when the non-renewal notice already says so.
That's the real problem: by the time anyone sees a warning sign, the decision is already final. There's no earlier signal anywhere in the business today.
The real data already exists, though, inside EVERPEAK_PROD, the live SQL Server database Renata Silva owns: accounts, subscriptions, usage events, support tickets, and invoices.
Dana Okafor sponsors this project, Renata knows the real data, and Tom Bellamy's team would be the one actually acting on whatever signal gets built here.
Next: turning 'stop the churn' into one precise, testable requirement, exactly what a 90-day warning sign has to mean.
